## Audits parallèles restants

Synthèse actionnable des constats reçus:

- P0 backend: poursuivre `ExecutionDriver` au-delà du contrat local initial avec drivers persistants/cluster/wasm et jobs durables; les jobs de run portent maintenant des metadata de campagne mais l'exécution reste locale.
- P0 backend: étendre la durabilité au-delà des payloads d'analyse locaux; SHAP et AutoML peuvent maintenant persister/recharger leurs sorties depuis le workspace, mais les jobs distants cluster/WASM et artefacts n4a-repo demandent encore un repository/driver durable de premier ordre.
- P0 backend: compléter la validation native réelle d'Inspector/Scanner/SHAP quand `nirs4all.pipeline.dagml.native_results` est disponible dans l'environnement de test; plusieurs tests natifs restent skipped localement.
- P0 frontend: migrer progressivement l'éditeur vers `EditorGraphDocument` comme source de vérité; les helpers de summary/diff existent et le handoff expérience transporte maintenant un document graphe, mais les composants éditeur restent majoritairement legacy.
- P0 frontend: faire évoluer l'exécution pipeline editor au-delà du modèle single dataset / regression-centric, en s'appuyant sur les metadata de campagne et le contrat frontend existants.
- P1 backend: brancher progressivement les routes discovery/rerun/AutoML sur `ResultsRepository`, `DatasetRepository`, et artefact repositories; scanner natif, dataset-scores et results-summary repository existent maintenant, mais rerun/delete et plusieurs routes restent très `StoreAdapter`.
- P1 backend: extraire un write-side repository pour run lifecycle / artefacts; `runs.py` n'utilise plus de SQL privé pour `project_id`, mais l'écriture begin/complete/fail reste `WorkspaceStore`.
- P1 frontend: terminer la normalisation/read-model Playground après le hotfix métriques; le contrat d'exécution transporte maintenant des observations structurées et le filtre métriques en consomme un read-model, mais les autres contextes/visualisations doivent encore adopter ce modèle.
- P1 frontend: consommer le bridge Inspector `MetricObservation` / `ScoreRef` dans les contextes et visualisations; le contexte de sélection métrique lit maintenant les observations, mais les visualisations doivent encore propager les shapes depuis les capabilities plutôt que depuis des hypothèses UI locales.
- P1 frontend: étendre le mapping `ScoreRef` au-delà des 5 colonnes legacy quand les protocoles/agrégations dag-ml complets arriveront.
- P2 frontend: stabiliser le hook/read model des résultats agrégés et faire dépendre le chart registry des capabilities disponibles.

## 2026-06-30 - Closing Audit: Residual Extension Risks (read-only, no code changes)

Read-only audit of the dirty worktree (1477 changed paths, branch `feat/native-results-reader`) before closing the pristine wave. Scope: maintainability risks that would obstruct the planned DAG-ML / multimodal / multitarget / cluster / campaign / result-meta-analysis extensions. Findings are observations only — nothing here was changed except this note.

Pipeline / DAG conversion (DAG-ML + multimodal):

- Linear-list pipeline model is baked into traversal on both sides: canonical root is `pipeline: Nirs4allStep[]` and is walked linearly (`api/pipeline_canonical.py` ~115-117/281-284; `src/lib/pipelineGraphSpec.ts` `walkSequence` ~169-262). Branching is synthetic nested containers, not first-class DAG edges — the single biggest blocker to a real DAG-ML graph. No explicit edge/dependency field exists on `PipelineStep` (`src/components/pipeline-editor/types.ts` ~70-82).
- Single-source assumption: `by_source` separation is a boolean flag and merges are positional/indexed (`merge: {predictions?, features?}`), with no named node/port routing (`src/utils/nirs4allPipelineTypes.ts` ~55-77; `api/pipeline_canonical_branch_merge.py`). Multimodal multi-source fusion ("feature out of A + prediction out of B") cannot be expressed.
- Duplicated god-function conversion: `_convert_step_to_editor` (Python ~1124-1279) and `convertStepToEditor` (TS ~116-215) are parallel 150+ line string-dispatch switches; a new flow/operator type must change ≥4 sites and risks silent Python/TS divergence. Registry/type fallback heuristics (`_infer_type_from_path` ~259-281) silently misclassify operators on non-standard class paths.

Inspector diagnostics (multitarget):

- The `score_ref` seam only reaches 2 endpoints (fold-stability, bias-variance). 10 POST endpoints (scatter/heatmap/candlestick/branch-comparison/confusion/robustness/metric-correlation/preprocessing-impact/hyperparameter/learning-curve) plus GET `/histogram` and `/rankings` are still bound to a flat single `score_column` (`api/inspector.py`). Branch-topology accepts `score_ref` only as a JSON query param, diverging from the POST-body pattern — two resolution conventions to maintain.
- Per-handler `_is_lower_better(metric)` reads the metric from a single chain record and assumes one metric across all chains — silently wrong on mixed-metric multitarget runs. `/metric-correlation` (~1706-1926, 221 lines) and the candlestick/heatmap/branch handlers bundle load+aggregate+rank with no reusable per-target aggregator seam.

Results / campaign / meta-analysis (cross-run):

- Frontend already has a substantial campaign layer (`src/lib/campaign*.ts`, ~2.3k lines) but the backend has NO `campaign`/`run_group` table or cross-run query surface; runs persist as per-run manifests + a flat `runs` table. Any campaign/cluster/meta-analysis view must scatter-gather per run in Python.
- Sibling CV/refit chain identity is reconstructed by signature matching within a single `(run_id, dataset_name)` scope and is copy-pasted across endpoints (`api/store_adapter.py` ~721-832; `api/aggregated_predictions.py` ~590-674). No stable cross-run chain key blocks cluster/meta joins. Aggregation endpoints mutate rows in place through ordered steps (mark→enrich→fallback), hard to generalize to multi-run input.

Native results adapter (the new DAG-ML on-disk format) — `api/native_results_adapter.py`:

- The new native (dag-ml) format is still force-mapped BACKWARD onto the legacy chain-centric `v_chain_summary` schema. Since this audit, the adapter has been widened to preserve additive score maps, `variant_params.result_metadata`, and native `branch_path` / `source_index` when projected rows or manifest metadata carry them; the remaining load-bearing assumptions are `best_params=None`, `model_step_idx=0`, flat legacy `cv_val/test/train` scalar columns, and no first-class per-target score surface. This remains the highest-leverage place to widen before DAG-ML results land, since it is the read path Studio will increasingly depend on.

Net: the wave correctly added narrow seams (score_ref, source/target selectors, native-results read path), but the load-bearing assumptions — linear pipeline, partial source awareness, flat single-target score column, single-run result identity, legacy chain schema — remain. Recommended next targets, highest leverage first: (1) widen the native-results adapter schema toward per-target score/prediction payloads before more endpoints couple to the flat shape; (2) a first-class DAG edge model in the editor/canonical types; (3) a backend campaign/run-group persistence + cross-run query surface to match the existing frontend campaign layer.

- Updated `buildCampaignPipelineRefFromSteps()` to preserve `steps` for `inline` and `inline-pruned` refs while keeping `saved` refs lightweight and backend-resolved by id.
- Added `createRunGroup()` in the runs API client, posting `NativeExperimentLaunchPayload` directly to `/runs/run-groups` without the legacy `{ config }` wrapper.
- Added focused tests proving inline/pruned refs carry steps, saved refs do not, and the native run-group payload transport is unwrapped.

Validation:

- Targeted ESLint passed for campaign spec/adapter, runs API, and tests.
- Targeted Vitest passed for campaign pipeline adapter, runs API, and experiment execution adapter (`21` tests).

## 2026-06-30 - Next Backend Patch Plans

Native results adapter schema widening:

- Highest-leverage patch: stop dropping native score maps at `api/native_results_adapter.py`, where native summaries currently emit `cv_scores` and `final_scores` as `None`.
- Add additive native columns/payloads only: `cv_scores`, `final_scores`, `variant_params.result_metadata`, retained `score_refs`, and native `branch_path`/`source_index` only when projection data provides them.
- Widen prediction arrays and aggregated-prediction payload parsing so multitarget `y_true`/`y_pred` and per-partition scores can survive transport without immediate UI rewrites.
- Tests should use fake native readers where DAG-ML is not installed, and should change exact-schema assertions into “legacy columns preserved plus additive native columns typed.”

## 2026-06-30 - Campaign Run Group Backend Seam

Completed:

- Added `POST /api/runs/run-groups` accepting `NativeExperimentLaunchPayload` directly and returning a normal queued `Run`.
- Validates strict single-pair campaign splits: no skipped run ids, manifest count matches `splitSpecs`, one dataset/pipeline/run entry per split, backend/dataset/pipeline ids match their source ids, and inline/pruned pipeline refs carry executable `steps`.
- Builds the run from `build_campaign_run_group_execution_plan()` rather than recalculating `dataset_ids x pipeline_ids`, preserving explicit split order, per-entry `splitGroupBy`, inline/saved pipeline resolution, and variant expansion.
- Carries campaign-shaped execution metadata (`campaign_shape`, native payload version, source/skipped run ids, strict campaign count) through the existing run/job-record seam.

Out of scope:

- No real cluster scheduler or WASM worker lifecycle is implemented here; requested cluster/WASM backends still rely on the current local execution-driver fallback until real drivers publish state, logs, cancel/retry, and worker status.
- No first-class durable `campaign`/`run_group` table or cross-run query surface exists yet; the seam creates a normal Studio `Run` with grouped dataset/pipeline entries.

Expected validation:

- Keep the existing focused plan test for explicit split ordering and grouping.
- Add or run targeted backend route coverage for accepted run-group payloads plus rejected skipped ids, manifest/spec mismatches, empty specs, missing inline steps, missing dataset/pipeline ids, and runtime grouping failures.
- Keep frontend transport coverage proving `createRunGroup()` posts the native payload unwrapped; full lint/test suites are not required for this seam-only validation pass.

## 2026-06-30 - Run Group Hardening And Logo Restore

Completed:

- Restored `public/nirs4all_logo.png` from the real logo asset instead of the square icon asset, fixing both the static/React splash screens and the main sidebar logo because they already reference this public logo path.
- Changed explicit campaign run-group pipeline-run ids to use the strict split spec id, preventing collisions when multiple strict split specs come from the same source campaign/run id.
- Kept inline and inline-pruned run-group configs per split spec instead of caching them only by `pipeline_id`, so two strict specs may reuse a displayed pipeline id while carrying different pruned executable steps.
